key_insight: Predictive triboelectric nanogenerator design requires linking evolving real contact area and contact-dependent charge generation and decay to electrical output across length scales.
engineering_relevance: Coupling materials, interface mechanics and circuit behaviour can guide more reliable energy harvesters and self-powered sensors.
method: Reviews polymeric, inorganic, composite and natural materials against charge retention, compliance and durability requirements.
Assesses modelling from atomistic calculations and rough-surface contact mechanics to device electrostatics and equivalent circuits.
Organises applications by device scale and proposes staged validation of mechanics, electrostatics and circuit response.
evidence_signal: The review assesses model inputs, predicted quantities and experimental validation evidence, while advocating independent testing beyond calibration conditions.
watch_item: Prescribed surface charge, idealised geometry and nominal contact-area assumptions can limit predictions under realistic loading.
paper_title: Triboelectric nanogenerators across length scales: linking materials, multiscale modelling and applications
